content.text: The text combines historical biography, polemical accounts of Catholic persecution, scientific articles, and an excerpt from Scott’s *The Lady of the Lake*. It recounts the Duchesse d’Angoulême’s resistance, exile, and death; attacks alleged Catholic miracles, inquisitorial torture, convent abuses, and Roman persecution, describing prisons and trials in Goa, Macerata, Spain, Rome, Naples, and elsewhere. Escape narratives include fugitives reaching Switzerland, England, France, and America. Scientific pieces describe the ocellated pheasant, maidenhair tree, and an American wood collection. The literary section summarizes James V of Scotland and follows Fitz-James through the Trossachs to Loch Katrine, where Ellen Douglas welcomes him to her island home; later events involve Stirling Castle, Roderick Dhu, and King James.
